To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
elevation is the best predictor for phylogeny and most traits change.

(1) Elevation is the main environmental factor for explaining the variation of phylogeny, traits and community assembly patterns; (2) Phylogenetic and functional structures clustered at high elevation; (3) Some functional traits overdispersed while some conserved; (4) Convergent tendency along elevation; (5) The phylogenetic signal showed no clear change along environmental gradients; (6) The phylogenetically conserved traits are LDMC, maximum plant height, and
1) Elevation is the main factor for phylogeny and trait variation along environmental gradients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assembly mechanisms in large‐scale gradients.
the phylogenetic and trait‐based assembly mechanisms along environmental gradients.
the assembly processes of community along environmental gradients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
community assembly processes along large‐scale environmental gradient are deterministic and phylogeny and most traits show different patterns.
phylogenetic and trait‐based community assembly processes in this study area are mainly deterministic processes driven by environmental filtering and niche partitioning.
phylogenetic signal may not be a useful indicator for exploring community assembly processes in large‐scale gradients, while functional structure may be a useful indicator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

phylogenetic signal may be more stable along environmental gradients than phylogeny and trait performance, and the phylogenetic and traits performance along environmental gradients may not be independent with each others.
phylogenetic and trait‐based methods are complementary to detect community assembly processes in different scales and different environment conditions.
the assembly processes in community ecology may be more complicated and diverse than we expected.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the assembly mechanisms in large‐scale gradients are more deterministic than stochastic.
phylogeny and trait‐based approaches can be combined together to study community assembly mechanisms along large‐scale environmental gradient.
phylogenetic‐ and functional‐ based approaches may be useful to explore assembly mechanisms in environmental gradients.
